pr_title: server: support SRV records to find nodes from --join list
pr_body:
Previously, the server's `--join` CLI argument list was static, which required to restart nodes more frequently than it might be needed to maintain the list up-to-date in dynamic environments (e.g. Kubernetes).

This change adds the support of SRV records resolution via DNS. If any hostname from `--join` argument can be resolved as SRV record, the endpoints from the response  are added into the list of known peers instead of original one. In that case, the port from the original address is ignored. There is no requirement for specific format (service or protocol) of the record because of their variable format in Kubernetes.

Closes: #45789
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/45815)
This is the first iteration to get a feedback regarding implementation details.. Tests are incoming.

issue_context.title: server: use DNS SRV records before A lookups to find nodes in --join
issue_context.body:
Requested/suggested by @vladdy for CC infra: given the DNS names of nodes are changing over time, there is no stable value of --join that can be provided to all nodes.

To ensure that clusters can transition into new nodesets over time, it would be useful to have the lookup operate using SRV records instead.
comments:
Alternative / complementary ideas:

- use bonjour mdns discovery
- provide an API endpoint to retrieve node lists
Good thing is the Go library already has `net.LookupSRV` see http://networkbit.ch/golang-dns-lookup/#lookupsrv

review_comments: We have an IANA-assigned port number, so ideally we'd use it here: `_cockroach._tcp.$NAME`. Is that compatible with how k8s sets up its SRV records? If not, this suggests that we may want more options than just SRV or not-SRV (or I guess we could just ask users to pass in the `_cockroach._tcp` bit explicitly if they're using SRV records, but that's ugly and not really how SRV was designed to be used).
we discussed that - the point was to be able to transparently "upgrade" an existing cluster deployment to use SRV records without changing the orchestration values for the `--join` flags
